rules.title: Whole-value borrow blocks any field borrow
rules.statement: A field-path borrow of `x.p` is rejected if `x` is already mutably borrowed; a `&mut x.p` is also rejected if `x` has any active shared borrow.

rules.title: Field mutation legality from reference-typed root
rules.statement: When the root `x` of a field place `x.p` has reference type, mutation legality is determined by the reference TYPE not the binding's `mut`: a `&mut`-typed root permits `&mut x.p`; a `&`-typed (shared) root rejects `&mut x.p` (E0596); the mut-binding declaration check is skipped for reference-typed roots.

rules.title: &mut of a field requires a mut binding (non-reference root)
rules.statement: `&mut x.p` where `x` has a non-reference value type is rejected unless `x` is declared `mut` or is a function parameter.

rules.title: Field borrows conflict on overlapping paths
rules.statement: `&mut x.p` is rejected if any overlapping path `x.q` is already shared-borrowed; any new borrow of `x.p` is rejected if an overlapping path is already mutably borrowed. Two paths overlap when equal or one is a dot-prefix of the other; disjoint sibling fields do not conflict.

rules.title: Cannot borrow a moved value
rules.statement: Taking any borrow (shared or mut) of a value that has been moved is rejected.

rules.title: &mut requires a mut binding
rules.statement: Taking `&mut x` is rejected unless `x` is declared `mut` or is a function parameter.

rules.title: Any field borrow blocks a whole-value &mut
rules.statement: Taking `&mut x` is rejected if any field-path borrow (shared or mut) of `x` is active.

rules.title: &mut is exclusive with existing mut and shared borrows
rules.statement: Taking `&mut x` is rejected if `x` is already mutably borrowed, if another mut reservation is in flight, or (outside call-arg evaluation) if any shared borrow of `x` is active.

rules.title: Two-phase borrow reservation during call-argument evaluation
rules.statement: Inside function-call argument evaluation, a `&mut x` is taken as a reservation that is compatible with shared borrows of `x` created during the same argument evaluation, but is rejected if any shared borrow of `x` pre-exists from an outer scope. Two `&mut x` in the same call (overlapping reservations) still conflict.

rules.title: Shared borrow excludes an active mut borrow
rules.statement: Taking `&x` is rejected if `x` is already mutably borrowed or if any field of `x` is mutably borrowed; otherwise multiple shared borrows coexist.

rules.title: Move-path overlap semantics
rules.statement: Two dotted paths conflict iff equal or one is a dot-prefix of the other; reading a moved leaf, a path inside a moved subtree, or a parent containing a moved leaf are all uses of (partially) moved data, while disjoint siblings do not conflict.

rules.title: Re-initialization clears equal and deeper move records
rules.statement: Assigning a path `p` re-initializes `p` and all deeper paths `p.*` (clearing their moved state), but a shallower moved entry is NOT resurrected: assigning `o.i.s` does not un-move a moved `o.i`.

rules.title: Use of a partially moved value is rejected
rules.statement: Consuming a value with at least one moved field is rejected as use of a partially moved value; consuming an already wholly-moved value is rejected as use of a moved value.

rules.title: Cannot move a borrowed value
rules.statement: Moving `x` is rejected while `x` is mutably borrowed, shared-borrowed, has a mut reservation in flight, or while any field of `x` is borrowed (E0505); a successful move resets `x`'s state and records it as moved.

rules.title: Use of reference after referent leaves scope (E0597)
rules.statement: A reference/borrow-carrying binding whose referent local has gone out of scope is flagged dangling; the first subsequent use reports E0597 ('does not live long enough'), once per binding. A stored borrow never used after its referent dies is sound (NLL).
rules.divergence: Rust NLL E0597 conformant; line-granular release (DIVERGENCES B6 closed)

rules.title: Use of moved or mutably-borrowed value
rules.statement: A value-use of `x` is rejected if `x` is moved (use of moved value) or while `x` is mutably borrowed.

rules.title: Pattern bindings introduced into scope
rules.statement: A variant-data pattern injects each of its binding names into scope; a wildcard pattern binds its name into scope only when the name is non-empty and not `_`.

rules.title: By-reference match binding inherits scrutinee borrows
rules.statement: When a `match`-arm variant-data binding has reference type or borrow-carrying type, it inherits the scrutinee's borrow sources, so the borrow cannot be smuggled past the referent's scope via the binding. By-value bindings copy out and carry no borrow.

rules.title: Elided &self -> &T (or borrow-carrying) ties result to receiver
rules.statement: A method with a reference first parameter, a reference or borrow-carrying return type, and no explicit lifetime parameters has its result lifetime tied to the receiver (self-borrowing). A method with explicit lifetime parameters does NOT count as self-borrowing.

rules.title: Operator-desugared call self-borrowing by name agreement
rules.statement: For an operator-desugared/trait method call carrying an empty resolved symbol (e.g. `v[i]`, `*p`), the result borrows the receiver iff EVERY method with that unmangled name is self-borrowing; any disagreement or no match yields not-self-borrowing.

rules.title: Borrow-carrying types and transitive containers are escape-tracked
rules.statement: A `#[borrow_carrying]` type (e.g. WAny) is escape-tracked like a reference, as is any generic container whose type-argument is transitively borrow-carrying (`Vec<WAny>`, `Option<WAny>`, `Box<WAny>`). A residency-exempt laundered-escape type (`Held<T>`/`HeldAny`) is never borrow-carrying, including via its type-arguments. A raw pointer (no type-args) is not borrow-carrying.

rules.title: Value-local root of a borrow place
rules.statement: The dangling-root of a borrow/receiver place is found by walking one optional leading address-of-temp, then a field/tuple-index/index/deref projection chain to a terminal variable, where a raw-pointer deref stops the walk (pointee not tied to pointer's stack lifetime). The terminal must be a value local (not a parameter, not a tracked reference binding) for the reference to be considered dangling-on-escape.
rules.divergence: Rust parity (raw-pointer deref breaks provenance, cf. box_leak)

rules.title: Bare-place method receiver self-borrow conflict
rules.statement: A method call on a whole-variable (non-field) bare-place receiver borrowing `self` conflicts with a live borrow of that variable: it is rejected if the variable is already mutably borrowed, or (for `&mut self`) if it has active shared borrows or any active field borrow. A raw-pointer-typed root is unchecked; reference-typed roots are checked.
